prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1119; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident details, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where the collision happened?
A: It was at a signalized intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. I was in the left-turn lane heading to a shopping center on the far side.
Q: Which direction were you traveling, and what did the signal show when you started your turn?
A: I was going straight through the intersection on the main road, then turning left onto the side street. The light had turned yellow when I reached the intersection, and I started my turn on a green arrow.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before impact?
A: Not until the last second. A pickup came through from the opposite direction, and I heard the brakes before the crash.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.
Q: Did you notice any traffic control malfunction or obstruction in the intersection?
A: No. The signal seemed normal. There was a delivery truck parked near the curb, but it wasn't blocking my path.
Q: Where did you feel the injury?
A: My left wrist hit the steering wheel and the door frame. I've since been told it's fractured, and I'm wearing a splint now.
Q: Did you seek medical treatment the same day?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that afternoon, and they sent me for X-rays.
Q: Has anyone else been injured?
A: The driver of the pickup said he was fine, and I didn't see anyone else hurt.
Q: Is there anything you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm sorry for the damage, and I want to make sure my insurance is handled properly.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
